title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of a camera alert being treated as an identification. The system flagged a Camaro as stolen and linked to aggravated robberies, and that flag travelled straight into a felony traffic stop: guns drawn, two men handcuffed, a helicopter and at least five patrol cars on scene. The failure sits at the handoff between the alert and the stop, where a partial match on a vehicle became grounds to treat its occupants as armed suspects.

What would have caught it is the step the deputies themselves could not complete. The undercover unit saw a matching car but could not read its license plates, so the match rested on make and model rather than on a confirmed plate. A verified plate, or any second identifier, before the stop escalated would have separated the flagged car from the one Anthony and Julian were driving. The system was used outside the conditions under which a vehicle match can stand in for a suspect.

What is not established is any finding against the deputies. The sheriff's office has said supervisors will review body worn camera footage to check whether procedures were followed, and that review is not a conclusion. Julian's account of being pushed down and threatened with being shot is his allegation, and the complaint he and Anthony plan to file is not a ruling.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in Cypress, Harris County sheriff's deputies surrounded a Camaro driven by Anthony, 19, and his friend Julian, 19, after cameras flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies. Deputies drew guns, handcuffed both men, and Julian said a deputy pushed him down and threatened to shoot him. Neighbor video showed at least five patrol cars and a helicopter. Deputies soon realized it was the wrong car and the men were not suspects.

The sheriff's office said an undercover unit saw a matching car but could not read its license plates, so backup was called. Supervisors, including the district captain, lieutenants, and sergeants, will review body worn camera footage to check that procedures were followed. The men were given information on filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so. Anthony's mother plans to hire an attorney.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
